history.summary: A Krishna temple dedicated to Govinddeoji (Govind Dev Ji) in the ancient town of Todaraisingh, listed among the town's historic temples alongside those of Kalyanji, Raghoraiji and Gopinathji (see travelgypsies.in and the seq 2113 notes). FLAG - CSV town 'Bavadi' is wrong: the verifiable Govinddeoji temple is at Toda Raisingh town (Tripadvisor: 'Govinddeoji Temple, Toda Raisingh Town, Tonk, Rajasthan'; geocoder pin 'Govind Dev Ji Temple, Kekri Road, Todaraisingh 304505'), and no Govinddeoji shrine could be traced to a village called Bavadi (a village of that name does not appear in Uniara tehsil's 2011 census list). No published founding history for this specific temple; not to be confused with the famous Govind Dev Ji Temple of Jaipur (City Palace) or CSV row 2078. Coordinates from map geocode of the Todaraisingh temple address; approximate.

name: Govinddeoji Temple, Todaraisingh
town: Toda Rai Singh (CSV says Bavadi; actual town is Todaraisingh)
town_description: Toda Rai Singh (Todaraisingh) is an ancient, hill-surrounded town in Tonk district, Rajasthan, about 48 km from Tonk and 135 km from Jaipur. Noted for its archaeological significance, stepwells (Hadi Rani ki Baori, Isar Baori, Bhopat Baori) and over 50 historic temples, it is locally famous for 'ghatti, patti, bawdi, dawdi'.

travel.railway: Tonk has no railway station; nearest major railheads Jaipur (~135 km) and Sawai Madhopur (~85 km, verify)
travel.road: ~48 km from Tonk town by road; buses and taxis from Tonk and Jaipur
